messages:
mira: Ok team — I'm sketching a PRD/RFC for the new 'arbiter' fallback policy. Goal: keep Tier1 p99 latency < 300ms in-region, allow graceful use of compatible model variants (quantized/size) when capacity constrained, and respect customer residency + opt-outs. Need: clear scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases. Quick thoughts?

sean: Can we first align on tier definitions and hard/soft SLOs? customers keep asking for deterministic behavior.

mira: Draft tiers: Tier1 = paid SLA (enterprise + dedicated), Tier2 = standard hosted paid, Tier3 = free/low-priority. Hard rule: Tier1 should not be silently degraded to an external region or non-approved quantized model unless customer allows it.

anika: Ops note: any cross-region fallback must respect residency/legal flags. We'll need per-customer metadata: residency=true/false and allow_cross_region_fallback=true/false.

josh: Model compatibility idea: maintain a compatibility matrix per model family. Example chain: 7B_fp16 -> 7B_int8 -> 3B_fp16. Prefer same-arch/param family before switching to smaller families.

sean: Routing policy sketch: 1) same-region, same-tier, same-model-version 2) same-region, same-tier, compatible-quantized variant 3) same-region, lower-tier compatible 4) cross-region same-tier compatible (only if residency allows) 5) fallback to cached responses / rerank. Tie-breaker: prefer variants with closest perplexity delta threshold (< 2% quality drop).

mira: Acceptance criteria (working draft):
- Tier1 in-region p99 <= 300ms for 95% of 7-day windows.
- Fallback rate to lower compute for Tier1 <= 0.1% (unless customer opt-in).
- Fallback quality regression measure: mean eval delta < 2% on customer prompt set.
- No silent cross-region fallback for residency-locked customers.
- Streaming sessions: no mid-stream model switch without explicit client notification.

sean: Example policy snippet for RFC (YAML):
```yaml
policy_name: arbiter_default
priority_order:
  - same_region: true
    tier: exact
    variant_preference: [fp16, int8]
  - same_region: true
    tier: lower
    variant_preference: [fp16, int8]
  - cross_region: true
    allowed_if: customer.allow_cross_region_fallback == true
quality_threshold: 0.02 # max allowed eval delta
log_and_alert: fallback_event -> ops-alert
```

kai: Heads-up: two customers (AcmeCorp, FinCo) explicitly forbade quantized fallbacks in their contracts. We need opt-out at account level + UI flag.

anika: Monitoring & alerting proposals:
- metric: fallback_rate{tier,region} -> alert if Tier1 > 0.1% over 1h
- metric: model_mismatch_errors -> alert at >0.1%
- runbook: if fallback spikes, auto-rollback routing policy to previous stable config and page oncall.

sophie-bot: deploybot: created RFC draft PR #412: https://git.internal/rfcs/412 - initial text + policy snippet attached.

josh: Edge-case: streaming sessions with active KV cache. If we switch models mid-session, KV layout mismatch may corrupt continuations. Options: 1) avoid mid-stream switches, 2) if unavoidable, expire session and return human-friendly notice to client, 3) implement KV translation (hard). Recommend 2 for v1.

sean: Implementation checklist for launch:
- RFC merged + design signoff
- Compatibility matrix for top 10 model families
- Per-customer residency/opt-out flags in account metadata
- E2E test harness simulating node OOM / capacity pressure
- Canary in us-west-2 + eu-west-1 for 48h
- Docs + SDK examples for opt-outs and streaming behavior
- Alerting + runbook tested in staging

mira: Owners: sean = spec + routing impl, josh = compat matrix + model tests, anika = ops + alerts/runbook, mira = product + acceptance criteria. Target: PRD + RFC ready by next Tue (2026-03-24).

sean: I'll start a PR with the deterministic ordering and tie-breaker tests.

josh: I'll publish a first-pass compat matrix CSV and synthetic eval scripts.

anika: I'll add the alerts + create a pager playbook.

mira: Thanks all. Quick check: can folks react here when they pick up tasks?
